newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen extending profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen extending profit-taking.

text.p: Polish shares fell in lower trade and analysts saw the Thursday fall as the beginning of a deeper profit-taking correction, after the bourse gained 38 percent since mid-December, and stabilised in the last few sessions.
The main market's WIG index fell 2.3 percent, to 17,824.4, and turnover fell 10.2 percent to 224.6 million zlotys ($74.7 million) on all three markets as 66 issues fell, 12 rose and 10 were flat.
Analysts said the falls might be additionally fuelled by U.S Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Wednesday warning of a possible need to raise interest rates.

"Greenspan's warning provoked the profit-taking as domestic investors fear that big ones will pull out and those who invest globally could close their positions here while limiting their global equity exposure," said Remigiusz Tarka of IB Austria.
Some analysts said the expected falls might last several weeks and take the WIG index down by about 10 percent.
Cables maker Kable trade was suspended after Denmark's NKT Cables called public tenders for all shares in the firm.
Garment maker Prochnik jumped 9.3 percent after National Investment Fund (NFI) 12 announced a tender for the firm's shares to increase its stake in Prochnik to 32.9 percent.
Analysts said construction firm Espebepe soared 9.6 percent, extending its recent surge on speculation that a March 14 meeting of the ailing firm's creditors might result in a debt write-off deal.
